You are assembling a clinical visit note. The sentences of one note are listed below in random order with their section headings removed. File every sentence under one of these four headings: SUBJECTIVE, OBJECTIVE EXAM, OBJECTIVE RESULTS, ASSESSMENT AND PLAN. In the JSON, the headings are the keys subjective, objective_exam, objective_results and assessment_and_plan. Return each sentence ID under exactly one heading. Do not leave any sentence out and do not invent IDs.

<sentences>
S1: Birth weight 4 pounds 8 ounces.
S2: Complete ultrasound today.
S3: If there are abnormalities on the kidney ultrasound, we will determine the next steps and future follow-up.
S4: She was referred to nephrology by genetics who recommended renal screening tests.
S5: Her mother notes that she is doing better with drinking fluids and she urinates “a lot”.
S6: Additionally, she has been seen by a geneticist, orthopedist, ophthalmologist, and audiologist.
S7: The patient drinks Ripple Pea Protein milk instead of cow’s milk, water and water mixed with a small amount of juice.
S8: • Smith-Magenis syndrome.
S9: I will call patient with results and possible next steps.
S10: Several organ systems can be affected by this chromosomal deletion syndrome and congenital anomalies of the kidney and urinary tract have been reported in the literature.
S11: The patient is not ambulatory, did not sit up unassisted until 1 years old, and is currently crawling and attempting to take steps.
S12: Sibling: 9-year-old brother and twin sister.
S13: No known family history of genetic conditions, kidney failure, dialysis, or kidney transplant.
S14: The geneticist informed the patient's mother that patients with Smith-Magenis syndrome usually have kidney issues where “the kidneys fuse into one” and issues with their legs.
S15: The mom states that Katherine is shorter and seems chubbier related to her syndrome.
S16: She will be starting speech therapy in the next few weeks, and currently she is in occupational, feeding, and physical therapy.
S17: The patient has seen many specialists, including GI for severe reflux, a dietitian who recommended discontinuing consumption of cow’s milk, and a neurologist who diagnosed her with Smith-Magenis syndrome.
S18: She also has a 9-year-old brother who is diagnosed with autism.
S19: Presences of microphthalmia.
S20: Patient accompanied to appointment by her mother.
S21: Well-nourished female, slightly fussy when examined.
S22: Her twin sister is approximately the same size, and their weight is essentially the same, she is healthy, and the mom denies any known health concerns or diagnoses.
S23: Brother: 9 years old, positive for autism.
S24: Renal screening tests.
S25: Smith-Magenis syndrome.
S26: Katherine Lopez is a 22-month-old female, born at 34 weeks +3 days gestation, diagnosed with the rare Smith-Magenis syndrome and associated global developmental delays.
S27: We will obtain a kidney ultrasound screening today.
S28: The patient has approximately 8 to 10 wet diapers in a 24-hour period.
S29: Katherine is a 22-month-old former 34+3-week-old twin with Smith-Magenis syndrome.
S30: The family lives in Dallas, Georgia, so her follow-up should be at the Town Center location.
S31: Twin sister: absence of Smith-Magenis syndrome, no known health conditions.
S32: At birth, the patient weighed 4 pounds 8 ounces, exhibited difficulties during eating where she would stop breathing, and challenges regulating her body temperature; determined to be typical issues associated with premature birth.
S33: Extremities: Presence of mild hypotonia of lower extremities and the arms.
S34: Normal external female genitalia.
